text: America just voted. AI stocks just fell. Connected?
Tuesday, Democrats won the House and Senate, AP says, with a few races still counting.
Thursday, the Nasdaq fell five and a half percent.
So why? Reason one: AI lives in giant computer warehouses, called data centers.
Investors fear the election could slow building them. Fewer data centers, fewer chips sold.
Like a brick maker hearing the town might stop new houses.
asr: Like a brickmaker hearing the town might stop new houses.

text: Reason two: big tech is spending huge sums on AI, and profits look slower.
Like a lemonade stand that's worth less once sales slow down.
Reason three: worry about higher interest rates. Safe savings pay more, so some money leaves risky stocks.
Like kids leaving the candy line when the ice-cream truck shows up.
So, did the election cause it?
Partly. It was Thursday's spark. But the slide started before anyone voted.
Connected? Yes. But not the whole story.
